summary: Compatibility candidate enforces the six local protected collection boundaries and preserves existing production workflows. It deliberately retains broad whitelisted booking/inventory/user permissions required by existing frontend actions, so it is not comprehensive production hardening.

findings.issue: The supplied production catch-all allows whitelisted writes to backend-only receipts, planning, redemption and email delivery state. Adding deny rules alone cannot restrict this grant.
findings.recommendation: Addressed in the candidate: replace the catch-all and exclude all six protected collections, including descendant paths. Do not keep the old fallback alongside the candidate.

findings.issue: The checked-in local users rule permits anonymous document writes, including role changes used by isAdmin/isJury.
findings.recommendation: Addressed for this candidate: do not import unconditional local user writes. Existing production whitelist-based user writes are retained because staff login and user management use them. The active local rules file remains unchanged.

findings.check: Business logic versus direct client permissions
findings.issue: Whitelisted clients retain unrestricted booking/inventory writes/deletes and can bypass frontend paid-booking deletion and payment checks. The current non-manual Mark Paid and terminal deletion paths require direct access.
findings.recommendation: Retained compatibility limitation: migrate remaining client mutations to protected backend endpoints before denying direct writes; add field/type/state/identity validation wherever client writes remain.

findings.issue: Supplied production public users/whitelist reads remain, and can expose stored contact or role fields.
findings.recommendation: Retained to preserve the requested production behavior. A separate access/privacy review should first trace login and user-management dependencies.

findings.check: Update bypass, type safety and resource exhaustion
findings.issue: Protected collections deny all client mutation types, but retained legacy whitelist writes and jury score writes do not impose complete field/type/size constraints. Whitelisted actors also retain broader registration/scoring access than the narrow rules suggest.
findings.recommendation: The candidate verifies protected create/update/delete boundaries. Redesign legacy validation and trusted-staff authorization separately rather than claiming this merge enforces all domain constraints.
